correctness.rationale: The adjacency recurrence in the polynomial ring of k,lambda,mu proves exact class formulas. The nonedge quadratic has strictly negative discriminant and positive leading coefficient. R4(-x)>e^-x for x>=0 implies positive diagonal. The edge cubic has derivative discriminant strictly negative because 0<=b/a²<1/4 and 0<mu/a<1. Its unique positive root is the complete positivity cutoff. At h=1/k all entries are strictly positive from a nonnegative polynomial in P=A/k, so the bound improves on forward Euler. Standalone stdlib verification.py passes the symbolic identities and 9,768 exact matrix comparisons; finite checks do not substitute for the general proof.

The complete multipartite Taylor result covers complete equal multipartite SRGs, but not primitive SRGs such as Petersen/Paley/Shrikhande.
The new proof controls every pair class uniformly for arbitrary feasible (k,lambda,mu) and shows no late sign reentry.

originality.rationale: The inspected Horváth–Song–Terlaky first-zero procedure covers arbitrary Taylor updates in general but does not give the strongly regular cubic, prove positive nonedge entries at every positive step, or exclude later recovery. Horváth 2005 addresses general RK positivity and invariant cones but not the parameter classification. Brouwer–Haemers gives the adjacency algebra without a time-stepping positivity result. Related special cases on regular bipartite, triangular, and multipartite graphs do not imply the result for all strongly regular graphs. Multiple semantic research searches found no covering statement, subject to unindexed-literature risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed or inaccessible specialized strongly-regular-graph RK4 source could contain an equivalent root formula; source search cannot guarantee world-wide priority.
General first-root theories may allow an alternate short derivation; the graph-specific discriminant and monotonicity conclusions are nevertheless separately proved here.

value.rationale: The claim classifies an entire natural family of graph heat systems using only three local SRG parameters, with a proved invariant all-step nonedge sign and no positivity recovery. It supplies a sharp usable timestep for all realizations, including primitive graphs outside existing special families, and proves a universal strict advantage over the Euler positivity bound.
